newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN TOWN LOSES ONE FRIEND, GETS ANOTHER.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN TOWN LOSES ONE FRIEND, GETS ANOTHER.

text.p: The Belgian town of Vilvoorde near Brussels, in the headlines for the past two weeks over the shock decision of French carmaker Renault to shut its plant there with the loss of 3,100 jobs, got a new friend on Tuesday.
Vilvoorde was one of eight Belgian communes to be twinned with a Japanese town as part of a campaign to bring the communities closer together and promote business ties.
But the planners might have been a touch more aware of the sensitivities in Vilvoorde. Their choice for its Japanese twin was Komatsu -- an industrial town known primarily for producing vehicles.
